title: Mastering psql & Meta-Commands
description: Navigate, inspect schemas, benchmark queries, and automate database operations using the official psql CLI tool.

data.text: **`psql`** is the native interactive command-line terminal for PostgreSQL. Beyond executing SQL queries, psql includes powerful meta-commands (starting with a backslash `\`) that inspect schema catalogs, benchmark statement execution, and format output.

rows: List all databases with sizes, collations, and owners
List all tables in current schema with disk sizes
Describe table columns, indexes, foreign keys, and triggers
List all schemas within the database
Toggle expanded display (vertical column output, great for wide tables)
Toggle query timing (prints millisecond duration for every query)

data.title: Connecting and Inspecting Table Schema
data.content: Executing psql commands to connect and describe a table.
data.code:
# Connect to database
psql -U app_user -d app_development -h localhost -p 5432

# Turn on query execution timing
app_development=> \timing on
Timing is on.

# Turn on expanded display for wide tables
app_development=> \x auto
Expanded display is used automatically.

# Inspect table columns, constraints, and indexes
app_development=> \d+ users

# Run query from an external SQL file
app_development=> \i migrations/seed.sql

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `psql` is the fastest and most dependable tool for PostgreSQL administration.
Use `\d+ tablename` to inspect column types, constraints, and index details.
Use `\timing` to measure query execution duration directly in the console.
Use `\x` to read wide records vertically without text wrapping.
